items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell 1.11% to 7,718.94 Wednesday, its worst day since July, while the Nasdaq dropped 1.88% to 26,692.87.
items.why: A hotter-than-expected inflation report revived Fed hike fears, and worries about debt-funded AI spending hit tech stocks.

items.detail: September consumer prices rose **3.7%** from a year earlier, above the 3.6% forecast and up from 3.4%, with core inflation at 2.6%.
items.why: Gasoline jumped 9.1% in the month on Iran-war oil prices, accounting for over half of the rise.

items.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.2% after the report, then eased to about **5.10%** early Thursday.
items.why: Traders briefly priced roughly even odds of a Fed hike this month, then scaled those bets back.

items.detail: Korea's **Kospi** plunged about 7.7% to 5,548.78 by midday Thursday, wiping out Wednesday's rebound, as Samsung fell 9.5%.
items.why: The hot US inflation report and Wall Street's tech selloff hit memory-chip makers hardest.

items.detail: The **Nifty** slipped 0.44% to 22,622.70 Wednesday, giving back part of Tuesday's rally, though the Sensex opened about 244 points higher Thursday.
items.why: Rising wholesale inflation and higher crude oil prices weighed on sentiment.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell 1.93% to 2,729.53 Wednesday, entering a correction 11% below its August high.
items.why: Higher yields hurt small companies most because many carry floating-rate debt.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** fell to about **$81,550** late Wednesday, failing again below $84,000 and giving up Tuesday's recovery.
items.why: Hotter core inflation revived Fed hike bets, pushing traders out of risk assets.

items.detail: **Ether** dropped to about **$2,412** Wednesday evening, back near last week's lows after Tuesday's bounce.
items.why: Leveraged long bets were wiped out after the CPI report, even after ether ETFs ended a 10-day outflow streak.

items.detail: **Solana** slid to about **$104** Wednesday, slipping from Tuesday's $107 hold.
items.why: US spot Solana ETFs kept losing money, with outflows in eight of nine October sessions.

items.detail: **Gold** fell more than 1% to near **$4,100** Wednesday, its third straight losing session.
items.why: The hot CPI report lifted the dollar and real yields, raising the cost of holding gold.

crossCuttingTheme: Gasoline pushed by the Iran war drove inflation to 3.7%, raising the odds of a Fed hike and sending yields above 5.2%. Tech, small caps, Korean chipmakers, crypto and gold all fell together.
